subject: Post-call: StratusDocs embedding fit, recommended models & drift plan
messages:
From: Ari Patel <ari.patel@stratusdocs.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up + metrics we care about

Thanks again for the call this morning — good conversation and helpful framing on how Redwood would slot into StratusDocs' search pipeline. I promised a concise follow-up with the metrics and constraints we're evaluating so you can recommend a fit and an initial pilot plan.

Short background/context: our existing semantic layer uses 512-d vectors produced by an in-house model. We see reasonable relevance for short queries but poorer performance on long-form and paraphrase queries; drift over new contract templates is our biggest worry.

Key metrics we want to measure (feedback from Product/CS):
- MRR@10 and Recall@10 on our 1.2k eval queries (mix of short/long)
- Average cosine similarity distribution per query type (short vs long)
- False-positive rate at cosine threshold 0.7 for long-form queries
- Dimensionality/size tradeoff (256 vs 512 vs 1024) and downstream retrieval latency
- Sensitivity to synthetic paraphrase drift (we plan to run a 3-week drift sim)

Asking for from Redwood:
1) Recommended model(s) to run for an initial A/B (cost vs quality tradeoffs) and which quantization profiles to try.
2) A quick benchmark link or artifact we can review (examples, scripts, or CSV results).
3) Suggested prompt/embedding settings and any pre/post-normalization you recommend.
4) Pilot scope: tokens, rate limits, sample size, timeline to get first results.

Attachments: we've attached our small eval set (1.2k queries) and a sample index snapshot. Please let us know if you'd prefer us to share via Drive link instead.

Next steps: can you send a short recommendation doc and a proposed pilot timeline by EOD Wednesday PST? Also flag any data access or NDA/workflow needs.

Thanks — Ari
Ari Patel
Head of Search, StratusDocs
ari.patel@stratusdocs.com

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>

On Mon, Jun 28, 2027 at 10:02 AM Ari Patel <ari.patel@stratusdocs.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for the call this morning — good conversation and helpful framing on how Redwood would slot into StratusDocs' search pipeline.
> ...

Hi Ari — great notes and appreciate the clear metric asks. High-level recommendations below; attaching a short artifacts bundle (benchmarks CSV + prompt set) and a 1-page pilot plan. Links are at the bottom.

1) Recommended models (initial A/B):
- rw-embed-s1 (512d): our production balanced model — strong recall on paraphrase and long queries, reasonable latency.
- rw-embed-lite-256 (256d quantized int8): lower cost, faster retrieval; good for short queries but expect lower paraphrase recall.
- rw-embed-highdim-1024 (1024d): best quality on paraphrases and long-form similarity but higher compute + index size. Use only if your storage/latency budget allows.

2) Quantization/profiles: start with rw-embed-s1 + rw-embed-lite-256 for cost/quality spread. If you see regression on paraphrases, run a targeted 1024d trial on a 10% sample. We'll provide precompiled quantized kernels for Dedicated/Private deployments to avoid runtime surprises.

3) Prompt/embedding settings + normalization:
- Use mean-pooled sentence embeddings with L2 normalization for cosine retrieval.
- For long-form docs, chunk by semantic paragraph (approx 150-300 tokens) then aggregate by top-K chunk scoring per doc.
- Prompt set: we've attached prompt_set_v3.json (includes paraphrase augmentations and long-query canonicalization).

4) Benchmark artifacts:
- Drive link: https://drive.redwood/reports/SD-embed-bench-0627 (contains CSVs: MRR, Recall, cosine histograms across models + dimensionalities).
- Local CSV attached: stratusdocs_embedding_benchmarks_v1.csv (summary rows + raw pair scores).

5) Pilot scope & timeline:
- Phase 0 (3 business days): data ingest & index snapshot (you share sample data via Drive; we need read access).
- Phase 1 (7 business days): run S1 vs Lite-256 across your 1.2k eval queries, produce MRR/Recall + cosine histograms.
- Phase 2 (optional, 5 business days): 10% 1024d trial if paraphrase regressions observed.

6) Drift monitoring suggestion:
- Run weekly drift sims with synthetic paraphrases and track delta in MRR and cosine distribution quantiles. We can provide an automated watch job and alerts in Redwood Console.

Attachments included: prompt_set_v3.json, MAP_reco_notes.pdf, stratusdocs_embedding_benchmarks_v1.csv

If this plan looks good, I'll schedule a 30-min pilot kickoff for Thursday morning PST to align on data access and roles.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0132
